questions.q: What was the special talent of the mighty men who came to David at Ziklag while he was staying away from Saul, the son of Kish?
questions.a: The mighty men were Benjaminites who could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and shooting arrows from their bows.

questions.q: Who commanded some of the Benjaminite warriors who joined David?
questions.a: The commanders were Ahiezer and Joash, sons of Shemaah from Gibeah.

questions.q: Who was Ishmaiah, and who joined with him?
questions.a: Ishmaiah from Gibeon was one of the thirty greatest warriors and commanded them; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederah also joined David.

questions.q: Who were the descendants of Korah who joined David?
questions.a: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam were all descendants of Korah who joined David.

questions.q: Who else joined David from the town of Gedor?
questions.a: Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham, joined David from Gedor.

questions.q: What were the special traits of the Gadites who joined David at the stronghold in the wilderness?
questions.a: The Gadites were fighting men trained for battle who could handle the shield and spear, who were as fierce as lions, and who could run as swift as gazelles on the hills.

questions.q: What was the order of rank among the leaders of the Gadite warriors?
questions.a: Ezer was first, Obadiah second, Eliab third, Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth, Attai sixth, Eliel seventh, Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth, another Jeremiah tenth, and Machbannai eleventh.

questions.q: What did the sons of Gad accomplish in the land given to Israel?
questions.a: The sons of Gad not only crossed the Jordan after it had overflowed its banks, but chased away all those living in the valleys.

questions.q: What warning did David give to the men of Benjamin and Judah when they came to his stronghold?
questions.a: David told them they could join him if they had come in peace, but if they had come to betray him to his adversaries, then he would tell God to rebuke them since he had done no wrong.

questions.q: What was Amasai’s response to David’s warning?
questions.a: Amasai told David that they were all on his side and only wanted peace for whoever helped David, because his God was helping him.

questions.q: Why did the Philistines send David away when he had come over to the Philistines to fight in battle against Saul?
questions.a: The Philistines were afraid that David would desert back to Saul’s side and put their own lives at risk.

questions.q: Who were the men from Manasseh who joined David when he returned to Ziklag?
questions.a: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, another Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai joined David; they were leaders over thousands in the tribe of Manasseh.

questions.q: How did the men of Manasseh, who later became commanders in David’s army, help him?
questions.a: The men of Manasseh were fighting men who helped David by fighting against the roving bands of robbers.

questions.q: How did David’s army grow in size before he became king?
questions.a: Every day more men came to help David until his army became very large, like a great army.

questions.q: Why did all the armed soldiers for war come to David at Hebron?
questions.a: They came to David at Hebron to help him take over the kingdom of Saul, which was a fulfillment of Yahweh’s word.

questions.q: How many soldiers came from the tribe of Judah, and what weapons did they carry?
questions.a: 6,800 soldiers equipped with shields and spears came from the tribe of Judah.

questions.q: How many warriors came from the tribe of Simeon?
questions.a: 7,100 warriors came from the tribe of Simeon.

questions.q: How many men came from the tribe of Levi?
questions.a: 4,600 men came from the tribe of Levi.

questions.q: Who led the men from the family of Aaron, and how many men came with him?
questions.a: Jehoiada, a descendant of Aaron, led 3,700 men.

questions.q: For what was Zadok known?
questions.a: Zadok was a young, strong, and courageous man.

questions.q: How many men came from the tribe of Benjamin, the relatives of Saul?
questions.a: 3,000 men came from the tribe of Benjamin, and most of them had been loyal to the house of Saul until then.

questions.q: How many warriors came from the tribe of Ephraim?
questions.a: 20,800 warriors, well known in their clans, came from the tribe of Ephraim.

questions.q: How many men came from the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan?
questions.a: 18,000 men, chosen by name to make David king, came from the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan.

questions.q: For what were the two hundred leaders from Issachar known?
questions.a: They had understanding of the times and knew what Israel should do.

questions.q: How many soldiers came from the tribe of Zebulun, and how were they equipped?
questions.a: 50,000 experienced soldiers, equipped with every kind of weapon and completely loyal to David, came from the tribe of Zebulun.

questions.q: How many commanders and soldiers came from the tribe of Naphtali?
questions.a: 1,000 commanders came from the tribe of Naphtali, along with 37,000 soldiers carrying shields and spears.

questions.q: How many men came from the tribe of Dan?
questions.a: 28,600 men who knew how to fight came from the tribe of Dan.

questions.q: How many soldiers came from the tribe of Asher?
questions.a: 40,000 experienced soldiers came from the tribe of Asher.

questions.q: How many soldiers came from east of the Jordan River, and which tribes did they belong to?
questions.a: 120,000 soldiers with many kinds of weapons came from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the other half of the tribe of Manasseh, from east of the Jordan.

questions.q: Why did all the soldiers of Israel come to Hebron?
questions.a: They came to Hebron with the firm intentions to make David the king over all Israel.

questions.q: Who prepared the food and drink so the soldiers of Israel could eat and drink for three days while celebrating David becoming king?
questions.a: Their fellow Israelites had prepared it for them.

questions.q: What did the neighboring tribes bring to celebrate David becoming king?
questions.a: People from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food including flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep, because there was joy in Israel.

commentary.text: Those who came to David at Ziklag.

Verses 1–22 Here is an account of those who appeared and acted as David's friends, while he was persecuted. No difficulties or dangers should keep the sinner from coming to the Savior, nor drive the believer from the path of duty. Those who break through, and overcome in these attempts, will find abundant recompence. From the words of Amasai we may learn how to testify our affection and allegiance to the Lord Jesus; his we must be throughly; on his side we must be forward to appear and act. If we are under the influence of the Spirit, we shall desire to have our lot among them, and to declare ourselves on their side; if in faith and love we embrace the cause of Christ, he will receive, employ, and advance us.

When the throne of Christ is set up in a soul, there is, or ought to be, great joy in that soul; and provision is made, not as here, for a few days, but for the whole life, and for eternity. Happy are those who wisely perceive it to be their duty and interest, to submit to the Saviour Jesus Christ, the Son of David; who renounce for his sake all that is not consistent; whose earnest endeavours to do good are directed by the wisdom that God giveth, through acquaintance with his word, experience, and observation. If any man lack this wisdom, let him ask it of God, who giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not, and it shall be given him.
